temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. Ethan invites Gary to a weekend retreat, but Gary declines because of hospital work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is dedicated but dangerously overworked and that a break could help protect his health.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's refusal shows that his work obligations are intense and that he is resistant to stepping away, even when concerned friends intervene.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is seriously overcommitted and may need continued help or encouragement to address his health.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Concerned, worried, and disappointed that Gary will not take a break.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To keep encouraging Gary to rest and to find another way to help him reduce his work stress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked and stressed by hospital duties, and that he may be at the retreat but still unable or unwilling to relax.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's restlessness and avoidance suggest that his overwork is not only due to professional obligations; something deeper may be troubling him.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan suspects Gary is hiding personal problems or additional pressures beyond his hospital workload.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To confront Gary gently and offer nonjudgmental support so Gary can open up.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and the personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects Gary's overwork is driven by more than professional obligations and that Gary is burdened by hidden problems.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Ethan's suspicion is confirmed: Gary is dealing with new department pressure and personal challenges, which explains but does not justify his unhealthy overwork.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan understands the reasons behind Gary's behavior and believes Gary needs practical help finding a better balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary prioritize tasks, delegate responsibilities, and organize a healthier schedule.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan checks in with Gary. Gary reports making progress, feeling less overwhelmed, and even having time for a movie.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has been struggling with work and personal challenges but is trying to improve with Ethan's support; the outcome is still uncertain.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's reports and actions show real improvement, indicating that the support and changes are working.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is on a positive path toward better work-life balance and can continue improving with encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue checking in, offering support, and encouraging Gary's progress.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance and appears capable of managing on his own. Gary thanks Ethan for his support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has improved and is managing better, though he may still feel some need to support or check in on him.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes. Gary's sustained adjustment shows he no longer needs active intervention and can maintain a healthier balance independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is capable, stable, and able to manage his own work-life balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back while remaining available if Gary ever needs him.
